enum: JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies
JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies

evidence_quotes.quote: Entre enero y junio de 2018, mediante el uso de un dron profesional, se realizaron relevamientos ortofotogramétricos de los 57 asentamientos

a veinte habitantes de cuatro sistemas urbanos de asentamientos informales (Torres de Mesana, Cuesta Colorada, Violeta Parra y Los Lancheros), acotando la muestra de estudio con el objetivo de identificar las estrategias y formas de provisión de agua de cada asentamiento.
el cual representa un total de 124,15 hectáreas, frente a las 72,72 hectáreas catastradas por la ONG TECHO y el Ministerio de vivienda y Urbanismo (MINVU) (ver Figura 2).
Otro resultado fue que solo tres de los 24 sistemas urbano geográfico de asentamientos informales se encuentran fuera del límite urbano definido por el Plan Regulador

evidence_quotes.criterion: effect_estimate and outcome_flags (lack of infrastructure in ZIUF)
evidence_quotes.quote: no cuenta con ninguno de los 1.131 hidrantes de la red seca que tiene la ciudad, los 22 estanques de agua que identifica la autoridad, ni con un colector de aguas lluvias.
en un promedio mensual de 24.000 litros, cifra que supera el promedio nacional de consumo familiar de agua, que es de 19.000 litros mensuales.

country.comment: Study examines informal settlements in the city/commune of Valparaíso, Chile (with brief secondary literature examples from other Global South countries in the theoretical framework).
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title; PDF p. 2, Resumen; PDF p. 9, Metodología

effect_estimate.comment: Descriptive spatial/quantitative and qualitative findings reported; no inferential regression point estimates, confidence intervals, or p-values are estimated.
effect_estimate.value: Descriptive mixed-methods findings (no regression effect estimate/CI/p-value reported): (1) Official campamento cadastres exclude irregular-tenure settlements of fewer than 8 families, invisibilizing 67% of informal-dwelling territory in Valparaíso (124.15 ha uncadastred vs. 72.72 ha cadastred by MINVU/TECHO). (2) Across 117,196 commune dwellings (2017 Census), water/sewerage coverage is 97.3%, leaving 3,122 dwellings inside the urban boundary without drinking water or sewerage (plus informal settlements outside the boundary; 2,716 families live in 57 cadastred campamentos). (3) Although 21 of 24 informal settlement systems lie inside the Communal Regulatory Plan urban boundary where formal infrastructure is legally required, in the southwest Urban-Forest Interface Zone (ZIUF, 260–410 m.a.s.l.) the formal water/sewerage network stops at 260 m.a.s.l., leaving all 11 ZIUF informal settlement systems without piped water or sewerage and with 0 of 1,131 fire hydrants, 0 of 22 official water tanks, and 0 rainwater collectors. (4) In 9 of the 11 ZIUF systems, inhabitants rely on wells, springs, informal connections, and municipal tanker trucks costing USD 10 per 6,000 L weekly (~USD 0.0016/L, comparable to the private utility tariff of USD 0.0016/L but excluding sewerage and network maintenance), consuming an average of 24,000 L/month per family vs. the 19,000 L/month national average due to leaks in self-built storage/distribution systems, alongside uncertain water quality and irregular delivery.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 4, Introducción; PDF pp. 10–13, Resultados (Figures 2–5 & Footnote 14); PDF p. 14, Discusión final

mechanism_certainty.comment: Capped at 2 by the MMAT mixed-methods design ceiling; rated 2 because the authors directly empirically document the legal/administrative mechanisms (tenure-recognition barriers, the >=8-family official cadastre definition, urban-boundary vs. private concession network limits, and municipal tanker-truck provision) via GIS overlays of official tenure/utility/cadastre records, in-situ planimetric mapping, and inhabitant interviews.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF pp. 5–7, Introducción & Marco teórico; PDF pp. 9–13, Metodología & Resultados; PDF p. 14, Discusión final

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines privatized water property rights under the 1981 Water Code (property), irregular land tenure and >=8-family cadastre rules (tenure, documentation), feasibility certificates and urban-boundary/Plan Regulador Comunal service obligations (documentation, service_area, planning), tanker-truck water pricing vs. formal utility tariffs (fees), interim municipal tanker-truck water delivery (accommodation), and split responsibilities across private utilities, MOP/DOH, MINVU, MBBNN, and municipalities (institutional_fragmentation).
mechanism_flags.value: ELIGIBILITY, BURDEN, DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION, tenure, property, service_area, planning, documentation, fees, accommodation, institutional_fragmentation
mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF pp. 5–7, Introducción & Marco teórico (Footnotes 5, 6, 8–10); PDF p. 9, Marco teórico & Metodología (Footnotes 11–12); PDF pp. 10–14, Resultados & Discusión final

outcome_flags.comment: Analyzes lack of piped drinking water and sewerage coverage, formal vs. informal connections, household water consumption volumes (24,000 vs. 19,000 L/month), tanker-truck prices vs. formal tariffs (USD 10 per 6,000 L vs. USD 0.0016/L), uncertain water quality and storage contamination, and delivery irregularity due to rain and steep topography.
outcome_flags.value: water_access, sanitation_access, service_coverage, formal_connection, service_quantity, affordability, service_quality, service_reliability
outcome_flags.where_found: PDF p. 2, Resumen; PDF p. 6, Introducción; PDF pp. 10–13, Resultados; PDF p. 14, Discusión final

publication_year.comment: The journal issue header printed on every page (PDF pp. 1–15) states 'enero - abril 2020' and '(1) 2020: 151-165' (accepted 14/08/2019; note that the 'Cómo citar este artículo' box on PDF p. 1 prints '(2019)').
publication_year.where_found: PDF pp. 1–15, running issue header ('enero - abril 2020', '30 (1) 2020: 151-165')

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Primary mixed-methods study combining quantitative spatial/orthophotogrammetric and in-situ planimetric cadastre data with qualitative semi-directive interviews.

sample_size.comment: Multi-level primary and secondary sample across settlement, household/dwelling, and individual interview units in Valparaíso.
sample_size.value: 57 informal settlements surveyed by drone (grouped into 24 urban-geographic informal settlement systems, of which 11 systems in the Urban-Forest Interface Zone were selected for spatial analysis and 4 systems for in-situ planimetric cadastre); 20 inhabitants interviewed via semi-directive interviews across 4 informal settlement systems; 117,196 dwellings in Valparaíso commune (2017 Census secondary data; 2,716 families in 57 campamentos per TECHO 2018)
sample_size.where_found: PDF p. 4, Introducción; PDF p. 9, Metodología; PDF pp. 10–12, Resultados

study_design.comment: Authors explicitly describe a mixed-methods design ('investigación mixta') integrating primary spatial/quantitative data and qualitative interviews with official secondary spatial/administrative records.
study_design.value: Mixed-methods spatial and qualitative case study combining drone orthophotogrammetric surveys, GIS spatial overlay of official utility/tenure/cadastre records, in-situ planimetric cadastre of water storage infrastructure, and semi-directive interviews
study_design.where_found: PDF p. 2, Resumen; PDF pp. 9–10, Metodología
